reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring complete cord injury as 3 (it is 2).
name: Thoracolumbar Injury Classification and Severity Score (TLICS)

version.label: TLICS (Vaccaro et al. 2005)
version.detail: Morphology 1–4 + posterior ligamentous complex 0–3 + neurological status 0–3. Total 1–10. The AO Spine thoracolumbar classification is a separate (licensed) system.

purpose: Classifies thoracolumbar injuries and summarises features relevant to management.
intendedPopulation: Adults with thoracolumbar spine trauma, using CT, MRI and neurological examination.

calculatorNotice.title: Classification, not a surgical decision
calculatorNotice.message: The authors proposed treatment thresholds; management also depends on the patient, associated injuries and surgeon judgement.

resultStates.label: TLICS 4
resultStates.summary: Score 4: either approach in the authors' scheme.
resultStates.detail: Management depends on patient and injury factors.

resultStates.label: TLICS {total}
resultStates.summary: Score 5 or more: the authors' operative range.
resultStates.detail: Management depends on neurological status, associated injuries, patient factors and surgical judgement.

clinicalContext.text: Combines morphology, PLC integrity and neurology to classify thoracolumbar injuries.

clinicalInsights.text: Incomplete cord/conus injury scores higher (3) than complete (2), reflecting potential benefit from decompression.

limitations.text: Proposed thresholds are not a substitute for surgical judgement.

limitations: Does not include patient factors such as bone quality.

guideSections.what: A score from morphology, PLC integrity and neurology for thoracolumbar injuries.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score the most severe morphology, the PLC and neurology; sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Supports management decisions made with the full clinical picture.

sources.citation: Vaccaro AR, Lehman RA Jr, Hurlbert RJ, et al. A new classification of thoracolumbar injuries: the importance of injury morphology, the integrity of the posterior ligamentous complex, and neurologic status. Spine. 2005;30(20):2325-2333.
